meta.notes: Expected values are EXTERNAL references (NIST WebBook, IAPWS-IF97 steam tables, SVN App. C, CRC/Perry class values) — never engine output — so these vectors detect coefficient transcription errors, not just regressions. Groups: A gas Cp/H (Shomate+SVN), B water/IF97, C Watson latent heat, D phase determination edge cases, E formation-basis reaction consistency, F solveT_forH round-trips. Group G (MB-026..MB-040): module solvers via runModule — mixer, splitter, flash (Rachford-Rice), heat-exchanger, rotating (pump/compressor/turbine), conversion reactor; expected values are hand calculations from steam tables, published Antoine constants, ideal-gas relations, and Felder & Rousseau-class worked figures — never engine output. Group H (MB-041..MB-052): cstr / pfr / pfr-recycle — expected values are hand calculations from the standard ideal-reactor design equations (Fogler, Elements of Chemical Reaction Engineering; Levenspiel, Chemical Reaction Engineering): CSTR X = Da/(1+Da) family, PFR X = 1−e^(−Da) family, recycle-reactor closed form X_ov = 1 − E/(1+R−R·E) with E = e^(−Da0/(1+R)) — never engine output. Test chemistry is the mass-balanced model liquid reaction 2 C3H6(l) → C6H12(l) (cyclohexane; 2·42.081 = 84.162 vs 84.161 kg/kmol, closure −0.0012 % — deliberately visible in closure_pct) with pseudo-nth-order rate laws in C3H6; feed 520 kg/h pure C3H6 with params.rho_kgm3 = 520 gives v = 1 m3/h and Ca0 = 12.35712 kmol/m3 exactly. Group I (MB-053..MB-062): smr / atr reformer equilibria — expected values are INDEPENDENT hand calculations (Python, separate from the engine) of the simultaneous CH4+H2O⇌CO+3H2 and CO+H2O⇌CO2+H2 equilibria from the published K correlations the spec prescribes (Twigg, Catalyst Handbook: lnK1 = 30.114 − 26830/T [bar²]; Moe 1962: lnK2 = 4400/T − 4.036), with adiabatic balances closed on NIST WebBook Shomate enthalpies — never engine output — and each point is cross-anchored to a published reformer equilibrium chart/table figure named in its source field. Dry-composition tolerance 0.015 mole fraction (1.5 % absolute per spec); adiabatic T_out ±25 K covers the ideal-gas-steam hand calc vs the engine’s IF97 water route. Group J (MB-063..070, shift + methanator): expected values are independent hand calculations from the Moe WGS correlation and the Twigg/Moe pair in the methanation direction, with adiabatic outlets closed on NIST Shomate enthalpies (ideal-gas H2O) — never engine output. The engine resolves water on IF97 (saturated-vapor-at-T below the pure-water Tsat), giving a few K of route difference on adiabatic outlets, covered by the stated tolerances. Anchors: Twigg HTS/LTS windows and exit-CO bands, Appl/Ullmann methanator ppm spec, and the classic ~74 / ~60 °C-per-1% adiabatic-rise rules, which the balance reproduces at 74.7 / 61.1 K. Group K (MB-071..MB-078): binary McCabe–Thiele distillation + Kremser absorber/stripper (Step 16). Expected values are INDEPENDENT hand calculations, never engine output: distillation D/B from the exact overall + light-key balances; Rmin from the q-line pinch on the equilibrium curve evaluated by hand (q=1 and saturated-vapour q=0 cases); minimum stages from the Fenske equation at total reflux; and the benzene–toluene classic stage count cross-anchored to the Fenske/Gilliland–Molokanov shortcut (Nmin≈5.7, R/Rmin≈1.5 → N≈11 incl. partial reboiler). Absorber/stripper expected values come from the Kremser equation directly: N = ln[φ(1−1/A)+1/A]/ln A for the number of stages (φ = removable-solute ratio), the (A^{N+1}−A)/(A^{N+1}−1) fraction-removed form for the outlet composition, the A=1 degenerate limit N=φ−1, and the stripping-factor S=mV/L analogue. The benzene–toluene VERIFY vector (MB-071) reproduces the textbook stage count within ±1 and its staircase is exported in details.svg for the live M-T diagram. Group L (MB-079..MB-088, urea HP section + solids): the urea reactor is an EMPIRICAL ESTIMATE, so its expected values are an INDEPENDENT evaluation of the tuned correlation held in Supabase correlation_params key 'urea_x_co2' (separate Python script, never engine output), combined with closed-form atom balances on 2NH3+CO2->carbamate, carbamate->urea+H2O and 2urea->biuret+NH3. Each vector is additionally cross-anchored to a named plant band (conversion 60-64 % at N/C 3.0 and 66-70 % at N/C 3.5; reactor melt 33-38 wt% urea; stripper bottoms 50-60 wt% urea; HP stripping steam 0.6-0.9 t/t; centrifuge cake 3-8 wt% moisture; dried product 0.2-0.5 wt%). Steam properties are external steam-table anchors, which makes MB-084/MB-085/MB-087 double as IF97-port checks. MB-082 deliberately sits OUTSIDE the validity envelope and asserts that all three breaches are flagged while a result is still returned. MB-083 asserts energy_balance.Q_kW is identically zero in adiabatic mode - the identity that proves the prescribed -117 / +15.5 kJ/mol reaction heats are live rather than decorative. MB-088 is a structural closure test on the HP loop: the carbamate recycle is the converged Wegstein tear and is internal, so C_in = 23 and N_in = 52 kmol/h must leave in the product streams. IMPORTANT: MB-079..MB-083 are frozen to the CURRENT correlation coefficients; retuning correlation_params is expected to break them, and their expects must then be updated deliberately. Group N (MB-089..MB-102, Step 21): PR φ–φ and NRTL flashes checked against the independent open-source thermo 0.6.1 library run with identical parameters (Tc/Pc/ω, H2 effective constants, kij); component splitter by hand calculation; whole-flowsheet solver and design specs by structural closure and the frozen template air rate; MB-103 checks the Step-21 dew-point vapour rule against a CoolProp/IAPWS-95 hand calculation of a wet-gas cooler + knock-out (−313.2 kW; the pre-fix engine gave −98.2 kW). Group P (MB-196..MB-207, Step 26): the Steam / water (IAPWS-IF97) package and the machine specifications — every expected value is computed with the independent Python iapws library (IAPWS97 class) for the same states: heater duties across regions 1, 2 and 3 (supercritical), outlet ρ / cp / μ / λ, turbine power and exhaust quality by efficiency, by measured outlet temperature and by shaft power, the extraction turbine section by section, a boiler feed pump, a vapour-recompression compressor, and the client's steam-turbine example flowsheet; MB-205/206 check the refusals (mixture, efficiency above 100 %). MB-095 and MB-100 were re-referenced when water Psat moved to IAPWS-IF97 (see their source fields). Group Q (MB-208..MB-219, Step 27): aqueous MDEA package (Extended UNIQUAC, Sadegh 2013 DTU thesis parameters) — MB-208..216 reproduce the thesis's own model results (Tables 7-13..7-17) as bubble pressures, MB-217 checks speciation against an independent Python implementation of the same model, MB-218 the heat of absorption against Oscarson et al. (1995) calorimetry. Group R (MB-219..MB-224, Step 28): activated MDEA (piperazine added to the MDEA package, its species fitted to measured data) — CO2 pressures over 7 m MDEA/2 m PZ and 5 m MDEA/5 m PZ (Chen 2011; the 5/5 set was held out of the fit), 7:2 MDEA/PZ and aqueous PZ at 120 °C (Xu 2011), a bubble pressure against Xu's measured total pressure and a density against Frailie (2014); tolerances 35 % on CO2 pressure reflect the fit's scatter. Group S (MB-225..MB-230, Step 32): free water in Peng–Robinson against IAPWS-95 (CoolProp) heater, boiling and 100 bar condensing duties; CO2 solubility in water against IAPWS G7-04; a near-critical flash against thermo 0.6.1 (substitution alone stopped at its iteration limit there); the energy-balance reconciliation flagging a classic unit next to Peng–Robinson units. MB-108/110/111 compare the raw cubic code-to-code with thermo, so they switch free water off.

vectors.source: Çengel & Boles (Thermodynamics) worked example class: theoretical adiabatic flame temperature of CH4 with stoichiometric air, complete combustion, no dissociation ≈ 2330 K (variable ideal-gas cp)

vectors.desc: cstr: first-order liquid, V→X — Da = kτ = 2 → X = 2/3 (Fogler CSTR design eq.)
vectors.source: Fogler (Elements of CRE) first-order liquid CSTR: X = Da/(1+Da), Da = kτ = (2/7200 s⁻¹)(7200 s) = 2 → X = 2/3; Ca0 = 520/42.081 = 12.35712 kmol/m³. Hand calculation.

vectors.desc: cstr: second-order liquid, X→V — τ = X/(k·Ca0·(1−X)²) = 16185 s, V = 4.4958 m³; batch-time equivalent 3237 s
vectors.source: Fogler CSTR design eq., 2nd order liquid: τ = X/(k·Ca0·(1−X)²) = 0.8/(1e-4 · 12.35712 · 0.04) = 16185 s → V = τ·v = 4.49583 m³; Da₂ = kτCa0 = 20. Batch/PFR equivalent t = X/(k·Ca0·(1−X)) = 3237 s. Hand calculation.

vectors.desc: cstr: Arrhenius k(A=1e5 s⁻¹, Ea=50 kJ/mol, T=350 K) = 3.4519e-3 s⁻¹ → Da = 12.427, X = 0.92552 (40 bar keeps C3H6 liquid)
vectors.source: Arrhenius: k = A·e^(−Ea/RT) = 1e5·exp(−50/(0.008314462·350)) = 3.45186e-3 s⁻¹; τ = 3600 s → Da = 12.4267; first-order CSTR X = Da/(1+Da) = 0.925522 (Fogler). Hand calculation.

vectors.desc: cstr: adiabatic + Arrhenius (dilute 5 % C3H6 in cyclohexane) — formation-basis identity Q ≈ 0 with converged T↔X loop
vectors.source: Formation-basis adiabatic identity: with T_out solved from stream enthalpies, the reported duty Q = Hout − Hin must return ≈ 0 (reaction heat is implicit in the formation enthalpies); exothermic-CSTR T↔k(T)↔X damped loop must converge.

vectors.desc: pfr: first-order liquid, V→X — X = 1 − e^(−kτ) = 1 − e⁻² = 0.86466 (exact per-segment march)
vectors.source: Levenspiel / Fogler PFR design eq., first order constant density: X = 1 − e^(−kτ) = 1 − e⁻² = 0.864665. Hand calculation.

vectors.desc: pfr: second-order liquid, X→V — kτCa0 = X/(1−X) = 4 → τ = 3237 s, V = 0.89917 m³
vectors.source: Fogler PFR design eq., 2nd order liquid: kτCa0 = X/(1−X) = 4 → τ = 4/(1e-4 · 12.35712) = 3237 s, V = 0.899167 m³; PFR ≡ constant-volume batch, so the batch-time equivalent equals τ. Hand calculation.

vectors.desc: pfr: zero-order liquid — X = kτ/Ca0 = (1e-3 · 5040)/12.35712 = 0.40786
vectors.source: Levenspiel zero-order design eq. (identical for PFR and batch): X = k·τ/Ca0 = 1e-3 · 5040 / 12.35712 = 0.407862. Hand calculation.

vectors.desc: pfr: axial profile — first-order X(z) = 1 − e^(−Da·z); at z = 0.5 (profile index 25 of 50), X = 1 − e⁻¹ = 0.63212
vectors.source: First-order PFR axial profile X(z) = 1 − e^(−Da·z), Da = 2: X(0.5) = 1 − e⁻¹ = 0.632121, X(1) = 1 − e⁻² = 0.864665. The exact-per-segment march must reproduce the closed form at every profile node.

vectors.desc: pfr-recycle: R = 50 approaches the CSTR limit — closed form X_ov = 1 − E/(1+R−R·E) = 0.67102 (CSTR: 2/3)
vectors.source: Recycle-reactor closed form (Fogler Ch. 6 / Levenspiel recycle reactor), first order: X_ov = 1 − E/(1+R−R·E), E = e^(−Da0/(1+R)), Da0 = kV/v_fresh = 2; R = 50 → X_ov = 0.671024, X_sp = 1 − E = 0.038457 — approaching the CSTR limit Da/(1+Da) = 2/3 as R → ∞. Iterations expected ≤ 30 with bounded Wegstein.

vectors.desc: pfr-recycle: R = 0 degenerates to a single PFR pass — X_ov = X_sp = 1 − e⁻²
vectors.source: Levenspiel recycle-reactor limit R → 0: plug flow, X = 1 − e^(−Da0) = 1 − e⁻² = 0.864665; single pass, no tear iteration.

vectors.desc: pfr-recycle: Wegstein-vs-analytic identity, R = 1, Da0 = 2 — tear fixed point must equal the first-order closed form
vectors.source: First-order recycle identity: X_ov = 1 − E/(1+R−R·E), E = e^(−Da0/(1+R)); R = 1, Da0 = 2 → E = e⁻¹, X_ov = 1 − e⁻¹/(2−e⁻¹) = 0.774600 and X_sp = 1 − e⁻¹ = 0.632121. The Wegstein-converged tear must land on the analytic fixed point (bounded q ∈ [−5,0]).

vectors.desc: pfr-recycle: adiabatic loop (dilute exothermic feed, R = 2) — envelope identity Q ≈ 0 at the converged tear incl. temperature
vectors.source: Adiabatic recycle envelope identity on the formation basis: mixing point and reactor both adiabatic → fresh-in / product-out duty must return ≈ 0 at the converged tear. Exercises the Wegstein tear including its temperature variable; iterations expected ≤ 30.

Eng. Prog. 58(3), 1962). Conditions of Speight fig. 7-3 (steam reforming equilibrium at 20 atm, H2O/CH4 = 3): dry CH4 slip ≈ 7.6 % at 800 °C, matching the published chart.

vectors.desc: smr fired: pure CH4, S/C = 3, 20 bar, 1000 °C, ATE 0/0 — near-complete CH4 conversion (published charts: conversion “complete at about 1,000 °C” at 20 atm)
vectors.source: Hand equilibrium calculation from Twigg lnK1 / Moe lnK2 (see MB-053). Anchor: Speight fig. 7-3 (20 atm, H2O/CH4 = 3) — “methane conversion is complete at about 1,000 °C”; dry slip 0.43 % reproduces the chart’s end point.

vectors.desc: smr fired: CH4 + 2 H2O, 1 bar, 1300 K, ATE 0/0 — SVN Ex. 13.14 conditions: reforming essentially complete, product split set by the shift equilibrium
vectors.source: Hand equilibrium calculation from Twigg lnK1 / Moe lnK2 (see MB-053) at the conditions of Smith, Van Ness & Abbott Ex. 13.14 (industrial CH4 reforming, 1 bar, 1300 K, 2 mol steam per mol CH4), where SVN’s ΔG°-based solution likewise gives near-total CH4 conversion with the mixture governed by the water-gas-shift equilibrium.

vectors.desc: smr fired: pure CH4, S/C = 3.5, 30 bar, 800 °C, ATE 0/0 — ammonia-plant primary-reformer point: ≈ 9 % dry CH4 slip
vectors.source: Hand equilibrium calculation from Twigg lnK1 / Moe lnK2 (see MB-053). Anchor: published ammonia-plant primary-reformer outlets at ~30 bar / ~800 °C / S/C 3–4 run ≈ 9–10 % dry CH4 (Twigg, Catalyst Handbook, steam-reforming ch.; Appl, “Ammonia”, Ullmann’s Encyclopedia).

vectors.desc: smr fired: MB-053 conditions with approach-to-equilibrium ATE_smr = 20 K, ATE_wgs = 10 K — slip drops as the reformer equilibrium is evaluated hotter
vectors.source: Hand equilibrium calculation from Twigg lnK1 evaluated at T+20 K and Moe lnK2 at T+10 K — the approach-to-equilibrium convention for reformer rating (Twigg, Catalyst Handbook: reformer duty expressed as an ATE on the reforming reaction).

Q_kW must be identically zero: in adiabatic mode the anchored basis makes Q = Hout - Hin = 0 an exact identity, which is what proves the prescribed reaction heats are actually live. PLANT ANCHOR: a carbamate-solution-fed HP reactor rises 15-25 K from a 160-170 degC feed to 183-190 degC.

vectors.desc: hp-stripper with CO2 strip gas: 80 % carbamate decomposition, 85 % NH3 / 97 % CO2 stripping, 190 degC bottoms, 23 bar MP steam

For this vector D = 0.80*7.372 = 5.8976, NH3 to gas = 0.85*(20.48851+11.7952) = 27.44115, CO2 to gas = 0.97*(0.228+5.8976+6.0) = 11.76183, H2O to gas = 0.03*22.334981 = 0.67005 kmol/h. MP steam properties are EXTERNAL steam-table anchors: saturated steam at 23 bar(a) is quoted at 219.6 degC (492.7 K) with hfg about 1857 kJ/kg; the IF97 port reproduces 492.51 K and 1860.9 kJ/kg, inside the stated tolerance. vectors.desc: dryer specified_T: 2881.65 kg/h urea cake at 6 wt% moisture to 0.3 wt% product, 22 t/h air at 120 degC - evaporation, exhaust humidity, saturation margin
vectors.source: Exact hand arithmetic plus one external steam-table anchor. Dry solids 2881.6489*0.94 = 2708.75 kg/h; product 2708.75/0.997 = 2716.9007 kg/h carrying 8.1507 kg/h of water; evaporation 172.8989 - 8.1507 = 164.7482 kg/h. Dry gas 22000*0.99 = 21780 kg/h, so the exhaust humidity is (220 + 164.7482)/21780 = 0.017665 kg/kg dry gas. Exhaust mole fractions give y_H2O = 0.027570; with the published saturation pressure of water at 100 degC (1.0142 bar) the relative saturation is 0.027570*1.05/1.0142 = 0.02854, i.e. the exhaust sits well clear of the dew point. PLANT ANCHOR: urea prill/granule dryers finish at 0.2-0.5 wt% moisture on hot air of 100-140 degC.

vectors.desc: urea-hp-loop: 46 kmol/h fresh NH3 + 20 kmol/h fresh CO2 + LP carbamate recycle at 150 bar - Wegstein tear on the HP carbamate recycle, overall C/N closure
vectors.source: Structural closure test, not a point prediction. The carbamate recycle is the converged Wegstein tear and is INTERNAL, so at steady state every carbon and nitrogen atom fed as fresh NH3, fresh CO2 or LP recycle must leave in the stripped urea solution: C_in = 20 + 3 = 23 kmol/h and N_in = 46 + 6 = 52 kmol/h are exact by inspection, and both closures plus the overall mass closure must fall inside the 0.01 % spec limit. The reactor ratios and conversion are then checked against the MB-079 correlation band, and the specific figures against plant experience: HP stripping steam 0.6-0.9 t per t urea, reactor N/C near 3 with the LP recycle shown. NH3 specific consumption reads high (about 655 kg/t against a plant 575-590) because the free ammonia in the stripper bottoms leaves this module for LP recovery rather than being recycled inside it - a topology statement about the module boundary, not a model error.

vectors.desc: optimisation (STEP 36): the same search with the constraint T(S1) ≤ 340 K ends on the constraint — the exact penalty keeps the optimum feasible

vectors.desc: heterogeneous bubble point (STEP 41): nitrogen / ethane 0.5 / 0.5 at 30 bar, Peng–Robinson — below the bubble point the feed is two liquids (a nitrogen-rich and an ethane-rich one); the first vapour forms when the nitrogen-rich liquid boils
vectors.source: Consistency: at 124.5869 K the nitrogen-rich liquid of the liquid–liquid split is exactly at its own bubble point (three phases in equilibrium), and below it the two liquids have the lower Gibbs energy. Before round 11 the bubble-point solver failed here ("residual NaN"); DWSIM 10 SRK (no N₂–ethane k_ij) returns 124.864 K, the bubble point of the single liquid, which is itself unstable — the engine’s SRK with the same k_ij = 0 gives 124.871 K, the split then being nearly gone.

vectors.source: Consistency: at 104.2689 K the nitrogen-rich liquid of the liquid–liquid split is exactly at its own bubble point (three phases in equilibrium), and below it the two liquids have the lower Gibbs energy. Before round 11 the engine returned 101.000 K — the bubble point of the feed as one liquid, which at that temperature splits into two.

vectors.desc: heterogeneous bubble point (STEP 41): nitrogen / carbon dioxide 0.5 / 0.5 at 30 bar, Peng–Robinson — below the bubble point the feed is two liquids (a nitrogen-rich and a carbon dioxide-rich one); the first vapour forms when the nitrogen-rich liquid boils
vectors.source: Consistency: at 123.9135 K the nitrogen-rich liquid of the liquid–liquid split is exactly at its own bubble point (three phases in equilibrium), and below it the two liquids have the lower Gibbs energy. Solids are not modelled: carbon dioxide would freeze long before this temperature; the case checks the fluid-phase calculation only.
